name: Weak metrics: misreads a short-form vs long-form A/B tradeoff

scenario.title: A/B tradeoff: short-form watch time up, long-form down
scenario.problemStatement: A video platform tested putting short-form videos higher on the home page. Short-form watch time rose 15%, long-form watch time fell 4%, and total watch time is up 1%. Do you ship it?

clarificationQuestions: What is the primary success metric: total watch time, satisfaction, revenue?
How do monetization rates differ between short and long-form?
Creator ecosystem impact: long-form creator earnings?
coreHypothesesOrSegments: Revenue per user (ads load differs by format)
analyticalPath: Convert watch time effects into revenue and satisfaction
benchmarkOutline.synthesisModel: Ship/no-ship rubric with revenue, retention, and creator guardrails.

messages.text: We tested moving short-form videos higher on the home page. Short-form watch time went up 15%, long-form went down 4%, and total watch time is up 1%. Would you ship it?
Yes, definitely ship. Short-form went up 15%, which is way bigger than the 4% drop, so it's a big net win.
Those percentages are on different bases though. Long-form is most of total watch time.
Okay, but total is still up 1%, so it's positive. Any increase in watch time is good.
Is watch time worth the same in both formats?
I think a minute is a minute. People are spending more time on the platform, which means more engagement and they like it more.
What about revenue, or the creators who make long-form videos?
Revenue should go up with more watch time. Creators can just start making short videos if that's what people want. That's how platforms evolve.
Would you want to know anything else before deciding?
Not really, the data is pretty clear. Maybe how many users were in the test.
Okay, give me your final recommendation.
Ship it to everyone, because short-form watch time is up 15% and total is up. We should keep pushing short-form.
